changes: End each repair prompt with an explicit active-target response skeleton; accepted and sibling IDs remain context only.
Allocate up to 4096/6144/8192 output tokens by target count, under the existing 8192 maximum; refit input before each new dispatch against the current ordinary and total token pools.
Checkpoint the exact prepared prompt, original target mapping, local evidence aliases, allowed sources, output limit and request digest before dispatch.
Pending requests are restored rather than regenerated or reallocated. A settled response can be reused after a crash before the draft checkpoint; unknown calls remain blocked by the ledger.
Persist per-batch budget/capacity stops and do not automatically restart a stopped round.
Strip internal output-allocation metadata before provider dispatch, including the plain tracked-invoker path.
unchanged: No retry of empty or truncated responses

offlineReplay.boundary: Request admission replay only; no new model response or scientific approval is asserted.

coverage: Real SQLite ledger blocks unknown pending requests
Real settled response reused after draft-checkpoint failure
Pending prompt not rebuilt despite changed live budget
Active response targets match each real prompt batch
Per-batch output reservation and provider metadata filtering
Existing scope, cancellation, publication and recovery regressions

limitations: Budget or indivisible required evidence can still prevent later batches.
Smaller output limits may produce truncated responses, which remain rejected.
Prompt and output limits are frozen; live authorization and provider policy still apply at dispatch.
Actual model adherence and full DR0-DR5 content acceptance remain unverified for this version.
